correctness.rationale: Apéry Lucas factorization follows from digitwise binomial/carry criteria; Domb Lucas factorization follows from a four-way squared multinomial identity and multivariate Lucas. The base-five digit pair table is exact. In \(\mathbb Z[g]/(g^4-1)\), diagonal and zero-Apéry classes correspond to \((2+g)^L\) and \((3+g+g^2)^L-(2+g)^L\); fourth-root evaluations prove the exact formula. Append digit four for infinite occurrence. Checker validates 300 independently summed indices and all displayed sample levels.

value.rationale: The result gives the entire indexwise two-sequence residue distribution of two classical sequences at the smallest prime where one has zero digit classes and the other has only unit digit classes. Exactly eight possible pairs, infinite occurrences, and an exact nonuniform conditional bias give a complete natural arithmetic invariant. It is not framed as a new Lucas congruence or a mere digit lookup.
